title: Choosing a message queue
brief: The Fulfillment team at Saltmarsh Foods needs to choose a message queue for the new order-routing service and wants a decision page for the architecture review on 2026-10-21. Expected load: 1800 messages per second at peak, 400 on average, messages under 8 KB, at-least-once delivery is acceptable, and ordering is needed only per order. Section titled "Options": SQS, Kafka (Amazon MSK) and RabbitMQ (Amazon MQ), one line each. Section titled "Comparison" as a table with a row per option and columns Ordering, Throughput ceiling, Ops burden, Replay, Monthly cost: SQS: FIFO per message group, very high, none, no, 310 dollars; Kafka: per partition, very high, high, yes up to retention, 1450 dollars; RabbitMQ: per queue, medium, medium, no, 690 dollars. Add a bar chart comparing estimated monthly cost: SQS 310, Kafka 1450, RabbitMQ 690. Section titled "Pros and cons": for each option two or three pros and cons as lists (SQS: fully managed and scales automatically, but no replay and a 256 KB message limit; Kafka: replay and stream processing, but needs partition planning and broker upgrades; RabbitMQ: flexible routing, but we would own capacity planning). Section titled "Recommendation": recommend SQS with FIFO queues keyed by order ID, in a highlighted callout, and note that we will revisit if the analytics team needs event replay in 2027.

edit.request: Change the recommendation to Kafka, and add a warning that it needs a dedicated on-call rotation for the brokers.
